## About

I am currently a postdoctoral researcher in economics at [Télécom Paris](https://www.telecom-paris.fr/fr/ecole/departements-enseignement-recherche/sciences-economiques-sociales), affiliated with the Centre de Recherche en Économie et Statistique ([CREST](https://crest.science/)) and the [Institut Polytechnique de Paris](https://www.ip-paris.fr/). I am also an associate researcher at the [UMR Développement et Sociétés](https://umr-devsoc.pantheonsorbonne.fr/), and I teach at [École Polytechnique](https://www.polytechnique.edu/) and the Institut d'Études du Développement de la Sorbonne ([IEDES](https://iedes.pantheonsorbonne.fr/)).

I hold a PhD in economics from Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne. My research lies at the intersection of digital and development economics, with a focus on causal impact evaluation and geospatial data analysis. Beyond connectivity, my recent work explores the role of digital platforms and artificial intelligence in shaping labor market dynamics.

<!---

I am also strongly committed to teaching and research dissemination. I designed and taught an advanced course on R programming and climate data analysis, and I regularly contribute to training sessions, workshops, and student supervision. My work is embedded in collaborative research projects, including the ANR JuGe project on marital dispute resolution in West Africa, and I am actively involved in networks such as ITS, AFEDEV, and the *Evidence Policy Impact Lab*.

## Teaching

### 📊 Quantitative Methods & Econometrics

- <strong>Applied Econometrics</strong> (École Polytechnique, M1): A course focused on causal inference in social sciences. Topics include RCTs, IVs, RDD, diff-in-diff, event-study, matching, and synthetic control. I lead tutorials based on critical reading.

- <strong>Applied Econometrics</strong> (IEDES, M1): Regression techniques with a focus on nonlinearities, interaction effects, heteroskedasticity, and count/discrete choice models. The course includes theoretical sessions and seminars using R.

- <strong>Collection and analysis of quantitative and qualitative data</strong> (UFTAM, M2): Course on research design, survey techniques, and mixed data analysis. Includes a final empirical project using R.


### 🌍 Development Economics & Policy

- <strong>Development Measurement</strong> (IEDES, M1): Covers poverty, inequality, and well-being indicators; measurement issues and aggregation/comparison methods.

- <strong>Development Economics</strong> (IEDES, M1): TDs covering core theories, development aid, and public policy.

- <strong>Conferences on policy and project in development</strong> (IEDES, M2): A professionalization-oriented course involving guest talks from alumni and practitioners from institutions like the World Bank, AFD, OECD, and NGOs.


### 📋 Data Science & Replication

- <strong>Climate and Data</strong> (IEDES, M2): A course I fully designed, teaching R and QGIS for climate and development data analysis. Includes data scraping, visualization, and geospatial mapping.

- <strong>Data Exploration and Modelling</strong> (IEDES, M1): STATA-based analysis of African firm survey data, focusing on gender wage inequality and labor discrimination.

- <strong>Tutored Projects in Development Economics</strong> (IEDES, M2): Replication of the paper “This Mine is Mine! How Minerals Fuel Conflicts in Africa” (Berman et al., 2017) using R and STATA. Covers geospatial data, modeling, reproducibility, and empirical presentation skills.
